newsitem.title: USA: Brent offers into U.S. fizzle, Oseberg talked.
newsitem.headline: Brent offers into U.S. fizzle, Oseberg talked.

text.p: Talk of bringing North Sea Brent crude to the Gulf Coast fizzled on Monday, although Oseberg as well as a variety of West African crudes were still on the table, traders said.
The April spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent was steady at around $1.60 cents a barrel Monday afternoon.
Last week's flurry of Brent offers had no takers, and buyers suggested that most of the talk was speculative anyway.
"People have stopped talking about (Brent)," one Gulf Coast refiner said, suggesting that Oseberg was gaining more attention at the moment.
A European company was showing the Norwegian light, sweet crude for delivery April 1-5, asking April WTI minus five cents a barrel.
A panoply of West African crude, including Bonny Light, Forcadoes and Qua Iboe, was still available.
Qua Iboe was on offer on a cost and freight basis for mid-April delivery at the equivalent of Dated Brent plus $2.05 a barrel, traders said.
Meanwhile, fresh offers of Iraqi crude were heard. An unnamed company was offering second-half April delivery of Basrah Light, asking May WTI minus $2.10 a barrel.
Bayoil was still showing an April cargo, asking April WTI minus $2.00 a barrel.
In Latin America, Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP was seeking to buy gas oil, 95-octane gasoline and jet fuel for early April delivery to cover ongoing work at the La Teja refinery, traders said.
Colombian Cusiana crude was heard done several times last week at May WTI minus 20 cents a barre, traders said.
